newsitem.title: USA: PECO seeks refinancing of generating assets.
newsitem.headline: PECO seeks refinancing of generating assets.

text.p: PECO Energy Co said Wednesday it filed a plan with the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) to refinance $3.6 billion of its generation-related assets.
The refinancing, if approved by the PUC, could result in nearly a $100 million, or an average 2.9 percent, annual reduction in customer electric bills, the utility said.
The rate reduction could possibly begin by the summer of this year, it added.
PECO said it is the first utility to formally seek "asset securitization" under a new Pennsylvania law.

Securitization is a mechanism that allows utilities to refinance some of their previous investments at substantial cost savings, which then could be passed along to customers. PECO also said its application was the first such request of this magnitude in the nation.

Several states, it noted, are moving toward electric industry deregulation with plans involving utility "asset securitization." And plans have been approved in California, New Hampshire and Rhode Island, in addition to Pennsylvania.

One of the first proposals was made in New York. Although it has not cleared that state's legislature, this proposal served as a model for the California and Pennsylvania laws, officials of both states said.
In Pennsylvania, the securitization is part of the Electricity Generation Customer Choice and Competition Act. The Electric Competition Act, which was signed into law by Gov. Tom Ridge on December 3.

If the Pennsylvania commission approves a second, more detailed PECO application, which will be filed this spring as part of the utility's restructuring proposal, the company estimates another rate decrease after completing refinancing of the remaining $3.5 billion of generation-related assets.
The total $7.1 billion to be refinanced represents PECO's total stranded assets, spokesman Neil McDermott said.
A timely regulatory order is critical for PECO to promptly reduce its customer bills, the utility pointed out.
The savings from refinancing with the prevailing lower interest rates will translate into lower costs, its statement explained. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
